「親愛的，等下要不要去享受一下。」羅一臉迷濛的送出訊息。

那張照片只是好看。
距離不遠。

「享受？我們不需要先吃個飯嗎？」

「對我來說那就是吃飯。」羅飛快打字，同時又已經滑向下一張照片。

自從被前任女友-克里娜（Krina）封鎖，她的時間變得更加空閒了。

ChatGPT
"Darling, want to go enjoy ourselves later?"

Rotlinde sent the message with a dreamy look on her face.

The photo was pretty. That was all that mattered.

And the distance wasn't bad, either.

"Enjoy ourselves? Shouldn't we get something to eat first?"

"That's what eating is to me."

Rotlinde typed the reply almost immediately, her fingers already moving toward the next profile before the conversation had even settled.

She had always been efficient about these things.

Since her ex-girlfriend, Krina, had blocked her, Rotlinde had found herself with considerably more free time.

Well, she assumed she had been blocked.

The evidence was fairly convincing.

Rotlinde stared at the screen for another second, then gave a small shrug and continued scrolling through the dating app.

The woman in the next photo had an interesting smile.

Her thumb paused.

"Hm."

Rotlinde lowered her voice even though there was no one around to hear her.

"Potential."

Her long, pale-blonde hair fell over one shoulder as she leaned back, looking almost too composed for someone casually browsing a dating app like she was choosing something off a menu.

Another profile.

Another photo.

Another possibility.

Her romantic life had always moved quickly.

Meet someone. Get along. Get close. Lose interest. Find someone else.

Simple.

At least, that was how Rotlinde preferred to think of it.

Almost every day, Rotlinde would end up in the same hotel with a different woman, in the same kind of room.

Even the hotel staff knew her by now.

They would exchange glances whenever she walked through the lobby with someone new, then whisper among themselves once she was out of earshot.

"How many does she have?"

"Probably just temporary romances. All for show."

"She's unbelievable."

"Pretty women get away with anything."

Rotlinde occasionally happened to catch those whispers.

She never took offense.

If anything, she considered them a compliment.

Not every woman could casually arrange a different date whenever she felt like it.

Rotlinde certainly could.

Whenever she noticed someone watching, she had a habit of giving her head a light toss, letting her long, pale-blonde hair sweep dramatically over her shoulder.

It was effortless.

At least, that was how she wanted it to look.

"That's a little theatrical."

Someone whispered nearby.

"Pretty women get away with anything."

Rotlinde's lips curved faintly.

She didn't bother turning around.

There was no reason to deny it.

Her relationship with her former wife had been considerably less effortless.

Her ex-wife had been a noblewoman, and the two of them had argued often—sometimes over the smallest things, sometimes over matters neither of them could remember afterward.

They had loved each other once.

Or at least, they had loved each other enough to get married.

Despite all their arguments, Rotlinde still felt grateful toward her.

When her former wife later died suddenly from an illness, she left Rotlinde a considerable inheritance.

A very considerable inheritance.

Enough, in fact, to make working for a living seem almost unnecessarily complicated.

Rotlinde had spent the years since putting that inheritance to excellent use.

By doing absolutely nothing productive with it.

She had no office to report to.

No boss to answer to.

No schedule demanding her attention.

Just hotels, dating apps, attractive women, and an alarming amount of free time.

Rotlinde considered this arrangement for a moment.

Then she shrugged.

It seemed to be working.

As for settling down?

Rotlinde had barely escaped the clutches of marriage.

No one was going to drag her back into that swamp.

She was a free animal now.

If she wanted to eat, she ate. If she wanted to go out, she went out. And when night came, she got to decide for herself who would be lying beside her.

Most importantly, she no longer had to worry about wine bottles flying at her.

Life was wonderful.

As for her ex?

Rotlinde firmly believed that was only temporary.

One day, Krina would unblock her.

Then, sooner or later, a message would appear on her phone.

Something simple.

*Want to go out tonight?*

Rotlinde could practically imagine it.

She smiled to herself.

There was no need to rush.

She wasn't worried about it at all.

Not even a little.

After all, Krina had only blocked her.

It wasn't as though she had disappeared from the world.

Rotlinde leaned back, looking perfectly at ease.

She had freedom.

She had money.

She had plenty of women willing to spend a night with her.

And, most importantly, nobody could tell her what to do anymore.

That was the life she wanted.

So why would she ever give it up?

---

Another day.

Rotlinde opened her eyes.

The woman beside her was already gone.

"Hm..."

She felt almost hungover, despite not having touched a drop of alcohol.

Apparently, she had spent all her energy on something else.

Her entire body felt heavy as she slowly sat up.

Rotlinde laughed quietly at her own expense, then got dressed and prepared to leave.

Was living like this boring?

No.

Not boring at all.

If anything, Rotlinde only had one concern.

She just hoped the flowers on the dating app wouldn't run out too quickly.

She was getting rather greedy about eating them.
